title: No flying-general pin exists when a piece of either colour blocks the file
rationale: Both chariots are undefended and attack each other on equal terms, which the same-type exclusion makes a mutual attack rather than a chase, and the black chariot is not pinned: the white soldier on c2 also stands between the two kings on the c-file, and it defends neither a4 nor a5. A piece is pinned by the flying-general rule only when the two kings share a file and it is the only piece of either colour standing between them, so neither side chases and the repetition is neutral. Guarded fork correction P2, which landed at afec5690: before it the engine ruled this position wrongly, and this fixture is what says so.
